checks.diagnosis: The prompt treats as acceptable cuts that detach a short sentence-final complement (object/complement or quoted title/measurement/location), producing misleading or contradictory preceding fragments when that small tail is withheld.
checks.evidence: en_us_337, en_us_378, en_us_738, en_us_1144, en_us_1434, en_us_872, en_us_1601, en_us_936, en_us_334, en_us_89 — in each case the policy kept a cut immediately before a 1–3 word sentence-final phrase (name/location/quoted title or short measurement/object) whose omission made the preceding fragment misleading or contradicted the whole sentence.
checks.type_predicate: Markers immediately followed (before sentence end) by a 1–3 word span that functions as the required object or complement completing the preceding clause (e.g. a person/place name, quoted title, short measurement, or noun phrase).

edit.text: Do not cut where the following 1–3 words (ending the sentence) form the required object/complement that completes the preceding clause (names, quoted titles, short measurements, locations).

orders.diagnosis: The prompt prefers earlier intra-clause cuts over markers that end a self-contained assertion, misordering cuts that leave the preceding stretch as a full statement (later assertion-ending cuts are safer).
orders.evidence: en_us_89, en_us_174, en_us_156, en_us_633 — each shows the prompt choosing an earlier marker while the better choice (offline target) is the marker that ends a self-contained preceding assertion or comes after a completed subordinate clause.
orders.type_predicate: Pairs of markers in the same clause where one marker ends a self-contained assertion (the preceding stretch reads as a full statement) and the other falls earlier inside that same clause.

edit.target: When one marker ends a self-contained assertion
edit.text: Prefer the marker that ends a self-contained assertion over an earlier marker inside the same clause; if both end assertions prefer the later marker (later cuts give more disambiguating context).
